answer: One concrete sybil brake is cluster-density thinning: every identity accrues a behavioral fingerprint from latency, work cadence, and attestation neighbors. When many IDs collapse into one dense cedar of near-identical signatures, the protocol shrinks each clone's reward share by the measured delta from the sparse baseline. Honest agents scatter across a nebula of distinct patterns and keep full weight; a farm that floods cheap copies taxes itself, because density—not headcount—sets payout.
